claim: For every integer u in the Borwein-Mossinghoff list L of 237,807 integers u < 5*10^49 (the values that pass Corollary 3, Theorem 5 and Theorem 7 of arXiv:1306.0045 and were left with some tests not run), and for every sequence a_1,...,a_n of +1/-1 terms with n = 4u^2, some aperiodic autocorrelation c_k (1 <= k < n) has |c_k| >= 2; that is, no Barker sequence of length 4u^2 exists for any u in L.

quadruple.statement: For every u in L, no Barker sequence of length 4u^2 exists (equivalently, since n > 13 and even, no circulant Hadamard matrix of order 4u^2 exists with the extra Barker constraint p = 1 mod 4 on every prime p | u).
quadruple.stage: Cyclotomic integers: the character sums X = chi(D) in Z[zeta_{4u^2}] of a Hadamard difference set D in the cyclic group of order 4u^2, with |X|^2 = u^2; arithmetic of multiplicative orders modulo the primes of u (all <= 1.3*10^11, factorisation of u given by the list).

shape.objects: Finite: the explicit list L of 237,807 odd integers u < 5*10^49, each given with its prime factorisation (every prime = 1 mod 4, largest prime 188748146801-scale, at most 17 prime factors with multiplicity); for each u the finite set of +1/-1 sequences of length 4u^2, never enumerated (4u^2 > 10^33).
shape.quantifiers: Universal over the finite list L, and for each u universal over all +1/-1 sequences of length 4u^2; a finite conjunction of decision problems, one per u.
shape.target_quantity: A decision per u (nonexistence of a Barker sequence of length 4u^2), delivered as the subset of L that is decided, each with a checkable arithmetic certificate; not a constant, exponent or density.
shape.ambient_structure: Two kinds of structure coexist: the combinatorial object (a circulant +1/-1 matrix with orthogonal rows, equivalently a (4u^2, 2u^2-u, u^2-u) difference set in Z_{4u^2}) and the arithmetic of the cyclotomic field Q(zeta_{4u^2}) (prime ideal factorisation of u, Galois action, orders of primes modulo primes, Wieferich pairs q^(p-1) = 1 mod p^2). The simpler ambient that keeps the constraint: the arithmetic necessary conditions on u alone, each a statement about the primes of u decided by modular exponentiation.
shape.symmetries: On sequences: reversal, negation, alternating negation; on difference sets: translation and multiplication by units of Z_{4u^2}; on character sums: the Galois group of Q(zeta_{4u^2}) (abelian) and complex conjugation; self-conjugacy of a prime p modulo m (p^j = -1 mod m') is the invariant that decides which prime ideals above p are fixed by conjugation.
shape.configuration: Required configuration: a +1/-1 sequence of length n = 4u^2 with |c_k| <= 1 for all 1 <= k < n; for n > 13 it forces a circulant Hadamard matrix of order n. It is an algebraic relation: X = chi(D) in Z[zeta_{4u^2}] with X*conj(X) = u^2 and coefficients in {0,1}, for every nontrivial character chi.
shape.extremal_candidate: Not applicable: the claim asserts nonexistence. The known Barker sequences have lengths 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 13, each unique up to the symmetries; no candidate of length > 13 has ever been exhibited.
shape.finite_certificates: The nonexistence side has a finite certificate per u: a parameter tuple for one of the known necessary conditions (Turyn 1965: (r, s) with r | u, s | 4u^2, r self-conjugate mod s and rs > 2^(k-1) 4u^2; Leung-Schmidt 2012 Thm 3.1: (m, w) with m self-conjugate mod 4u^2/w and 4u^2 phi(F) > w^2 F^2; Leung-Schmidt 2012 Thm 3.5: (p, r) with gcd of orders > m^2/r^2; Leung-Schmidt 2016 Thm 6.3: (d, p, q) with ord_p(q) > q^(4b) max(...)), each checked by modular exponentiation modulo primes <= 1.3*10^11 and exact big-integer comparison, polynomial in log u once the factorisation is given (the list gives it). The existence side has the sequence itself as certificate, of length > 10^33, never expected.
shape.monotonicity: No monotone parameter: the list is a finite set with no order that the tests respect. The list is stratified by Omega(u) in {2,...,17} and every known test loses power as Omega(u) grows (Turyn's test eliminates 91.7% of the list at Omega = 4 and 3.8% at Omega = 8). The smallest open value is u = 30109*1128713*2167849*268813277 (Leung-Schmidt 2016).
shape.uniformity_parameter: Omega(u), the number of prime factors counted with multiplicity: the naive implementations of Turyn's test and of Leung-Schmidt 2012 Thm 3.1 enumerate divisor pairs and run in time exponential in Omega(u), which is why Borwein-Mossinghoff ran Turyn's test only for Omega(u) <= 8 and Thm 3.1 only for Omega(u) <= 6; 226,913 of the 237,807 values have Omega(u) >= 9.
shape.proof_shape: Per u, a chain of necessary conditions with no induction: existence => for every nontrivial character a cyclotomic integer X with |X|^2 = u^2 and coefficients in {0,1} => (self-conjugacy, field descent, or anti-field-descent) X, or a twisted product X^sigma X / w, lies in a small subfield or fails to, forcing an inequality between u, a divisor of u, and multiplicative orders of primes of u => the inequality fails for the actual primes => contradiction. Each step is a finite computation given the factorisation; the loss per step is the slack of the inequality (e.g. the factor 2^(k-1) in Turyn's bound, the max term in (109) of Leung-Schmidt 2016).
shape.neighbours: (a) The Barker conjecture for all even lengths: open. (b) Ryser's circulant Hadamard conjecture: open; arXiv:2302.08346 (Morris 2023) and arXiv:1907.12683 (Orozco Lopez 2019) claim proofs, neither accepted (Leung-Schmidt 2016 still lists u = 11715 as the smallest open order). (c) Odd lengths: settled (Turyn-Storer 1961; Schmidt-Willms 2016). (d) The complete range 13 < n <= 4*10^33: settled, no Barker sequence (Leung-Schmidt 2016 Thm 6.4). (e) The 19 values with n <= 10^50 in the list: all settled (Leung-Schmidt 2016 Table 1). (f) The sublist with Omega(u) <= 6 (541 values): every test of Borwein-Mossinghoff 2014 was run on it; Turyn's test for Omega <= 8. (g) The same statement for the whole list: 229,682 of the 237,807 settled by Leung-Schmidt 2016 Thm 6.3, 8,125 open (their list unpublished). (h) The circulant Hadamard analogue for u <= 10^13: 1371 open after Borwein-Mossinghoff 2014, 423 of them settled by Leung-Schmidt 2016. (i) Gallardo arXiv:1411.2201 and arXiv:1411.2203 (2014) claim that no circulant Hadamard matrix of order 4h^2 exists for 1 < h < 10^13 and that ord_{n/p^a}(p) must be odd; unrefereed and not adopted by the field.
shape.known_bounds: No Barker sequence of length n with 13 < n <= 4*10^33 (Leung-Schmidt 2016, Thm 6.4; Borwein-Mossinghoff 2014 had one exception, now removed). On the list L: Corollary 3 (p^(3l) <= 2u^2), Theorem 5 (u phi(u) <= F(u^2, u)) and Theorem 7 (p = 1 mod 4) hold for all 237,807 values by construction; Turyn's test (Thm 2) was run for Omega(u) <= 8 and eliminated 1045 values; Leung-Schmidt 2012 Thm 3.5 was run on all values and eliminated 4; Leung-Schmidt 2012 Thm 3.1 was run for Omega(u) <= 6 and eliminated 2; Leung-Schmidt 2016 Thm 6.3 was run on all 237,807 and eliminated 229,682, leaving 8,125 (smallest: 30109*1128713*2167849*268813277); this attack reconstructed the 8,125 survivors with certificates for the 229,682 (enumeration-run-1). Documented ceilings: Turyn's test needs, for each prime of r, every other prime of s in one 2-adic class of the order (so it fails once the primes of u spread over several classes, which is why its yield falls with Omega(u)); Thm 6.3 needs a prime p of u whose 'source' primes (Wieferich pairs (r,p) or primes s with p | ord_s(r)) reduce to one prime q after removing a unitary divisor d with phi(d^2) < p phi(u^2)/(2u^2). Completeness of L beyond n = 4*10^33 is not claimed by its authors, so no lower bound beyond 4*10^33 follows from clearing L.
shape.missing_input: Not one missing lemma. The strongest known method (anti-field-descent, Leung-Schmidt 2016) was applied to L only in its prime-power special case (Theorem 6.3, u/m = q^b); its general form (Theorem 6.1, u/m with several prime factors and a free integer t) and the older tests (Turyn's Theorem 2 for Omega(u) >= 9, Leung-Schmidt 2012 Thm 3.1 for Omega(u) >= 7) have never been applied to the 8,125 survivors.
shape.base_theory: ZFC, in practice classical algebraic number theory (cyclotomic fields, Kronecker's theorem on algebraic integers, Gauss sums, Cassels' M-function) for the necessary conditions, and Peano arithmetic for every certificate check: modular exponentiation with moduli below 2*10^22, exact big-integer products and comparisons of numbers below 10^100. The difficulty starts at finite objects; no hypothesis beyond the base theory decides the statement or a neighbour.

known: Turyn 1965 (Pacific J. Math. 15, 319-346): if a circulant Hadamard matrix of order n > 4 exists then n = 4u^2 with u odd and not a prime power; the self-conjugacy test: r | u, s | n, gcd(r,s) with k >= 1 distinct primes, r self-conjugate mod s implies rs <= 2^(k-1) n.
Turyn-Storer 1961 (Proc. AMS 12, 394-399): no Barker sequence of odd length > 13; Schmidt-Willms 2016 (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 80, arXiv:1501.06035) give a shorter proof.
Eliahou-Kervaire 1992 (Enseign. Math. 38, 345-382): a Barker sequence of length n > 13 has constant periodic autocorrelation, so n is even and gives a circulant Hadamard matrix of order n.
Eliahou-Kervaire-Saffari 1990 (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 55, 49-59): if a Barker sequence of length 4u^2 exists then every prime p | u satisfies p = 1 mod 4.
Jedwab-Lloyd 1992 (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 2, 93-97): Corollary 3: if p^l | u then p^(3l) <= 2u^2.

Schmidt 1999 (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12, 929-952): field descent: X in Z[zeta_m] with |X|^2 = n satisfies X zeta in Z[zeta_F(m,n)]; Leung-Schmidt 2005 (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 36, 171-188, Cor. 4.5): u phi(u) <= F(u^2, u) for a circulant Hadamard matrix of order 4u^2.

Mossinghoff 2009 (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 53, 149-163, DOI 10.1007/s10623-009-9301-3): the directed-graph method (Wieferich pairs as solid edges, p | r-1 as flimsy edges); n = 189260468001034441522766781604 or n > 2*10^30.

Leung-Schmidt 2012 (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 64, 143-151, DOI 10.1007/s10623-011-9493-1): Thm 3.1: m | u, w | n, m self-conjugate mod n/w implies n phi(F(n/w, u^2/m^2)) <= w^2 F(n/w, u^2/m^2)^2; Thm 3.5: p | u, a = nu_p(u), p^(2a) > 2u, r | u/p^a self-conjugate mod p, q_i the primes of (u/p^a)/r, then gcd(ord_p(q_i)) <= (u/p^a)^2/r^2; Thm 3.10 for primes = 3 mod 4 (not Barker-relevant); the single open case below 2*10^30 removed.

Borwein-Mossinghoff 2014 (LMS J. Comput. Math. 17, 24-32, DOI 10.1112/S1461157013000223, arXiv:1306.0045): n = 3979201339721749133016171583224100 or n > 4*10^33; the list L of 237,807 values u < 5*10^49 (file BarkerCandidates100.txt, Wayback capture 2021-07-18 of wayback.cecm.sfu.ca/~mjm/WieferichBarker/); Table 100: Turyn's test run for Omega(u) <= 8 (1045 eliminated), Thm 3.5 on all (4), Thm 3.1 for Omega(u) <= 6 (2); 549 values pass all tests among those tested.

Leung-Schmidt 2016 (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A, DOI 10.1016/j.jcta.2015.11.005, 'The anti-field-descent method'): Theorems 6.1 and 6.3 (twisted cyclotomic integers); Thm 6.4: no Barker sequence of length 13 < n <= 4*10^33; all 19 list values with n <= 10^50 eliminated (Table 1); Thm 6.3 eliminates 229,682 of the 237,807 values of L, the smallest survivor being u = 30109*1128713*2167849*268813277; the data for the survivors are 'available from the authors upon request' and are not published.

Logan-Mossinghoff 2017 (J. Combin. Math. Combin. Comput. 101, 145-156, 'Double Wieferich pairs and circulant Hadamard matrices'): later Wieferich-pair data for the circulant Hadamard problem (files AscWiefPairs_DWPCHM.txt, CHM_Candidates_DWPCHM.txt on the same site); abstract only, not read in full.

Gallardo arXiv:1411.2201 and arXiv:1411.2203 (2014), Morris arXiv:2302.08346 (2023), Orozco Lopez arXiv:1907.12683 (2019): claimed stronger nonexistence results or proofs of Ryser's conjecture; none refereed in a journal record found, none adopted by Leung-Schmidt 2016 or by the later literature; treated as unverified.

This attack, enumeration-run-1 (2026-09-02): Theorem 6.3 of Leung-Schmidt 2016 re-implemented and run on all 237,807 values with an independent checker; 229,682 eliminated and 8,125 survivors, matching the published counts and the published smallest survivor; the survivor list is now explicit (deterministic/enumeration-run-1/survivors_thm63.txt). Every survivor contains the four primes 30109, 1128713, 2167849, 268813277 (the cycle 30109 -> 1128713 -> 268813277 ~> 2167849 ~> 30109), only 35 distinct primes occur, and for every survivor and every admissible (p, d) at least one prime fails (108).
